n_basis_note: All segments, including trap TAN, are plotted on one 'N concentration (mM)' axis and stack to the initial N, and the paper's TAN recovery (Eq. S8) divides the trap-tank TAN concentration by the input nitrate concentration. That only conserves N if the trap tank volume equals the feed tank volume (feed tank 50 mL is stated; the trap tank volume is not stated) or if the authors normalized trap TAN to the feed volume. NH3_trap is therefore taken as trap-loop N per feed volume, mM-N equivalent; treat its absolute basis as unverified. NO3-, NO2-, TAN are plotted as N (axis 'N concentration'/'N species'; nitrate given as NO3--N in the text), so no N-atom conversion. Cross-check from the Fig. 2e run (same cell and protocol): the text's 'total molar amount of the generated NH3 was only 1.05 mmol' at 120 min (p. 11608) equals the plotted Fig. 2e TAN at 120 min, feed + trap = (7.72 + 13.54) mM x 50 mL = 1.06 mmol, so the authors express trap TAN per 50 mL of feed. That supports the mM-N-per-feed-volume reading but cannot tell equal tank volumes from normalization.

provenance.notes: Two-compartment system. The cathode loop (feed tank <-> cathode chamber, 50 mL/min) holds NO3-, NO2- and TAN ('TAN in feed tank' / 'TAN in reaction chamber' -> species NH3). Gaseous NH3 crosses the hydrophobic PTFE membrane into the trap chamber, whose 0.5 M Na2SO4 is recirculated (50 mL/min) through the trap chamber, the anode chamber (acidified by O2 evolution; Nafion 117 PEM between cathode and anode chambers) and the trap tank, where NH3 is held as NH4+ ('TAN in trap tank/chamber' -> species NH3_trap, kept separate, never added to NH3). Fig. 1a and Fig. S2a also show an air pump on the wastewater tank and a 'gaseous NH3' line from the wastewater tank to the trap tank, so NH3 may also reach the trap by headspace stripping; the text does not quantify that route. N2 was not measured: the authors computed it as initial N minus (NO3- + NO2- + TAN in both tanks) (SI Part S2) and plotted it as the top bar segment; it is stored as quality.reported_n_loss, not as a species, and our n_closure is 1 minus that gap. NO and N2O were assumed negligible by the authors (SI Part S2), not measured. METHOD: Raster digitization of the embedded Fig. S13 JPEG (SI PDF page 15, 1430x864 px, 220 ppi) (the figures are embedded raster images; there are no vector paths). Image extracted at native resolution with pdfimages; y axis calibrated by a linear fit to tick-mark pixel centroids located automatically (darkness profile beside the axis line) and assigned to the printed tick labels (all labelled and minor ticks, >=4 per panel, max tick residual <0.15 of one minor step); bars located at the x tick centroids. For each bar two side strips (avoiding the centred error bars and the outline) were classified pixel-wise by nearest colour prototype, the two orange TAN classes split by hue; segment boundaries come from a monotone dynamic-programming segmentation that enforces the legend's stacking order. Resolution 0.085 mM per pixel; boundary uncertainty about +/-1-2 px. Segments not visible are recorded as 0.0 (below ~1 px); values below ~0.2 mM (<=2-3 px) cannot be distinguished from outline/anti-aliasing artefacts. Error bars in the figure were not extracted. Extracted by agent team 2026-10-20; overlay of the extracted boundaries on the figure crop checked by eye (scratch, not committed).  Segment 'TAN in reaction chamber' -> NH3 (cathode loop), 'TAN in trap chamber' -> NH3_trap. Text: TAN selectivity 78.7-85.1% across -1.5 to -3.5 V; our end-of-run TAN/input: see the converter closure. reported_n_loss is the authors' by-difference N2 (initial N minus the measured species), so besides any real N2 it carries any reading bias of the stacked-bar tops (about 0.11 mM in Fig. 2e) and absorbs any NH3 stripped from the feed tank through the air line that does not end up in the trap. DC-on window presumed: Fig. S13 has no DC on/off shading or label (see conditions.notes), so the whole plotted period is taken as powered; this is an assumption, not a statement of the paper. conditions.catalyst: CuO-coated Cu foam (mixed-valence Cu2+/Cu1+ oxide layer) clipped to a PTFE/PP membrane (0.45 um), 4 cm2, as the electrified membrane cathode
conditions.electrolyte: synthetic wastewater: 25 mM NO3- (as N; KNO3) + 10 mM Cl- + 0.5 M Na2SO4, initial pH 7.0
conditions.potential_as_reported: -3.5 V vs SCE (no ohmic compensation; SCE +0.241 V vs SHE)
conditions.stirring: recirculation by peristaltic pumps at 50 mL/min (cathode loop: feed tank <-> cathode chamber; trap loop: trap tank -> trap chamber -> anode chamber -> trap tank)
conditions.notes: Three-chamber flow cell: trap | CuO@Cu-foam/PTFE cathode membrane | cathode chamber | Nafion 117 PEM | anode chamber (Pt mesh 3.5x3.5 cm); SCE reference in the cathode chamber; CHI 1100C potentiostat. volume_mL is the feed tank: 50 mL is stated in the text only for the Fig. 2e run (25 mM, pH 7, -2 V) and is assumed here, since the feed volume is not restated for this run; chamber and trap-tank volumes not stated. pH is the initial feed pH; in-run pH is not reported for this run. The text's in-run values, a strongly alkaline cathode loop (12.65 +/- 0.13, attributed to 'the trap chamber' in the text but in context the cathode side) and a final trap-tank pH of 1.53 +/- 0.10 after 120 min, are stated only for the 25 mM, pH 7, -2 V run of Fig. 2e. Current is not reported for this potential: the text's ~50 mA cm-2 (0.204 +/- 0.011 A, the mean over 0-120 min) is stated only for the -2 V Fig. 2e run, and Fig. 3a gives only normalized efficiency indicators, so no current can be derived for this run. RHE conversion not done: large uncompensated iR, and the in-run pH is not reported. Sampling 0-60 min, every 10 min. Fig. S13 does not mark DC on/off periods; the -2 V panel (S13b) shows only the 0-120 min DC-on part of the Fig. 2e run, so these panels are presumably all DC-on, but that is not stated.
